title: 3D Diagonal "Key Race Condition" Movement
body: ### Tested versions Reproducible in: Godot v4 (any v4 not just 4.6-beta1) Not reproducible in: have not tried any other version. ### System information Godot v4.6.beta1 - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Direct3D 12 (Forward+) - dedicated AMD Radeon RX 7700 XT (Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.; 32.0.22029.9039) - 13th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-13600K (20 threads) - 63.74 GiB memory ### Issue description When pressing W + D together for first-person movement, the expected result is continuous diagonal movement (forward-right combined). However, input appears to arrive in a rapid alternating order (e.g., W, D, W, D), causing movement to be applied forward first, then sideways (or “up then sideways” depending on the controller), instead of a stable combined vector. This feels like a key input “race condition” where the movement code receives key signals in a way that briefly treats the input as one key at a time rather than both held simultaneously. This is especially noticeable in FPS-style controllers and results in jittery / step-like diagonal movement. Expected: Holding W+D produces a stable diagonal movement vector every frame. Actual: Holding W+D can behave like forward motion followed by right slide (sequential), as if only one key is active at a time due to event ordering/repeat. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Create a new project (3D). 2. Add a CharacterBody3D (or Node) and attach the script below. 3. Run the scene. 4. Hold W, then hold D while still holding W (also try pressing them “together”). 5. Observe that the printed key events may alternate rapidly and/or movement becomes forward-then-right instead of diagonal. Minimal script (prints key event stream) ```gdscript extends Node func _input(event): if event is InputEventKey and event.pressed: # Print key stream and whether Godot marks it as echo/repeat print("key=", event.keycode, " pressed=", event.pressed, " echo=", event.echo) ``` script ```gdscript extends CharacterBody3D const SPEED = 5.0 const ACCEL = 10.0 # How fast you reach max speed const FRICTION = 15.0 # How fast you stop on the ground const AIR_RESISTANCE = 2.0 # How much control you have in the air const JUMP_VELOCITY = 4.5 const MOUSE_SENSITIVITY = 0.003 @onready var head: Node3D = $Head func _ready() -> void: Input.set_mouse_mode(Input.MOUSE_MODE_CAPTURED) func _unhandled_input(event: InputEvent) -> void: if event is InputEventMouseMotion: rotate_y(-event.relative.x * MOUSE_SENSITIVITY) head.rotate_x(-event.relative.y * MOUSE_SENSITIVITY) head.rotation.x = clamp(head.rotation.x, deg_to_rad(-89), deg_to_rad(89)) if event.is_action_pressed("ui_cancel"): if Input.get_mouse_mode() == Input.MOUSE_MODE_CAPTURED: Input.set_mouse_mode(Input.MOUSE_MODE_VISIBLE) else: Input.set_mouse_mode(Input.MOUSE_MODE_CAPTURED) func _physics_process(delta: float) -> void: # Add the gravity. if not is_on_floor(): velocity += get_gravity() * delta # Handle jump. if Input.is_action_just_pressed("ui_accept") and is_on_floor(): velocity.y = JUMP_VELOCITY # Get input direction var input_dir := Input.get_vector("strafe_left", "strafe_right", "move_forward", "move_backward") var direction := (transform.basis * Vector3(input_dir.x, 0, input_dir.y)).normalized() # Determine which logic to use: Acceleration or Friction var target_vel = direction * SPEED var accel_rate = 0.0 if direction: # We are moving accel_rate = ACCEL if is_on_floor() else AIR_RESISTANCE else: # We are sliding to a stop accel_rate = FRICTION if is_on_floor() else AIR_RESISTANCE # Apply the movement velocity.x = move_toward(velocity.x, target_vel.x, accel_rate * delta) velocity.z = move_toward(velocity.z, target_vel.z, accel_rate * delta) move_and_slide() ``` Note: Even if event-driven movement is not the recommended approach, the issue is that the input event stream can alternate rapidly in a way that makes “two keys held” appear like “one key at a time” unless additional filtering/debouncing is added. If this is expected behavior (OS repeat behavior), clarification/documentation or an engine-side mitigation (e.g., ensuring repeats are consistently flagged as echo, or guidance in docs) would help because it commonly affects FPS movement implementations. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [FIX] Input_Debouncer.gd: ``` extends Node @export var input_buffer_time: float = 0.04 var _last_confirmed_vector: Dictionary = {} # Stores buffered vectors by name var _buffer_timers: Dictionary = {} func _physics_process(delta: float) -> void: # This manager updates every physics frame to keep buffers in sync with states for map_name in _buffer_timers.keys(): _buffer_timers[map_name] += delta func get_buffered_vector(neg_x: String, pos_x: String, neg_y: String, pos_y: String) -> Vector2: var id = neg_x + pos_x + neg_y + pos_y var raw_input = Input.get_vector(neg_x, pos_x, neg_y, pos_y) # Initialize if not present if not _last_confirmed_vector.has(id): _last_confirmed_vector[id] = Vector2.ZERO _buffer_timers[id] = 0.0 # 1. Instant Spam Bypass if raw_input != Vector2.ZERO and (raw_input == _last_confirmed_vector[id] or _last_confirmed_vector[id] == Vector2.ZERO): _last_confirmed_vector[id] = raw_input _buffer_timers[id] = 0.0 return raw_input # 2. Diagonal Buffer elif raw_input != _last_confirmed_vector[id] and raw_input != Vector2.ZERO: if _buffer_timers[id] < input_buffer_time: return _last_confirmed_vector[id] # Return previous until buffer clears else: _last_confirmed_vector[id] = raw_input return raw_input # 3. Release/Idle else: _buffer_timers[id] = 0.0 if raw_input == Vector2.ZERO: _last_confirmed_vector[id] = Vector2.ZERO return raw_input ```
